channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Com Caiado, Renan e Cury, primeiro debate presidencial é marcado por críticas às ausências de Lula e Flávio
item.description: The first 2026 presidential debate, hosted by Band and Estadão, featured Renan Santos (Missão), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Augusto Cury (Avante), while Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro and Romeu Zema were absent. The candidates’ no-shows were criticized during the debate, which covered security, education and international relations.

item.title: Renan Santos afirma que Lula e Flávio deveriam falar no debate sobre 'crimes cometidos'
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) criticized the absence of Lula and Flávio from debates, stating they should attend to explain the crimes they have committed.

item.title: Em debate, Caiado diz que Lula tem espantado geradores de riqueza do Brasil
item.description: In a recent debate hosted by Band and Estadão, PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado criticized President Lula, claiming his administration has driven away wealth generators from Brazil. Caiado called for a credibility shock in the economy and pledged not to increase the country’s public debt if elected.

item.title: Debate Band/Estadão começa com púlpitos reservados a Lula, Flávio e Zema vazios
item.description: The Band/Estadão debate began with empty pulpits for Lula, Flávio, and Zema, with only Ronaldo Caião, Renan Santos, and Augusto Cury participating. The absence of the most popular candidates drew criticism regarding the debate's representativeness. Participants addressed topics such as economy and security.

item.title: Renan chama Lula e seus eleitores de canalhas: 'Não quero seu voto'
item.description: In the first presidential debate on Band, Renan Santos (Missão) called re-election candidate Lula (PT) and his voters 'scoundrels', stating he does not want their votes. The statement sparked strong reactions and highlighted the tense tone of the election.

item.title: Lula diz que não interfere na PF e defende investigação sobre o filho
item.description: President Lula stated in an interview with Record that he does not interfere with the Federal Police and supports investigations into his son, Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, who is under three inquiries. He emphasized that 'no one is above the law' for wrongdoing.

item.title: “Você será meu xerife”, diz Cury a Caiado, que nega convite
item.description: During a debate on Band, Augusto Cury invited Ronaldo Caiado to be the sheriff of Brazil in his potential government. Caiado declined, stating he intends to run for president.

item.title: “Lula vendeu com a mulher que estocava vento a ideia da Pátria Educadora”
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate from Missão, criticized the educational policies of Lula and Dilma's governments during a Band debate, mocking the 'Educating Homeland' idea with reference to Dilma's old 'wind farming' statement.

item.title: Cury abre live, declara ausência, volta atrás e participa de debate
item.description: Augusto Cury initially announced his absence from the first presidential debate on Band, citing the absence of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, but later reversed his decision to participate after press pressure. Lula, Flávio, and Zema also skipped the debate to preserve their campaign strategies.

item.title: Cury lamenta “nível de agressividade” de Renan e faz convite a Caiado
item.description: Augusto Cury criticized Renan Santos's aggressive tone during a public security debate on Band, and invited Caiado to broaden the discussion. The Avante candidate highlighted concern over the confrontational climate in the electoral scenario.

item.title: Bastidores: Zema priorizou estreia no Jornal Nacional e não quis virar ‘alvo das pedradas’ em debate
item.description: Romeu Zema chose his debut on Jornal Nacional over attending the first presidential debate, avoiding becoming a target in an unfavorable political showdown. The decision was made behind the scenes due to a tight schedule and the current electoral dynamics.

item.title: Datafolha: 50% acreditam em possível interferência de outros países nas eleições no Brasil
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows 50% of voters believe foreign interference in Brazilian elections is possible, while 43% do not believe in this hypothesis.

item.title: Sem Lula, Flávio e Zema, candidatos fazem primeiro debate à Presidência
item.description: The opening presidential debate featured only Augusto Cury (Avante), Renan Santos (Missão) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Flávio Dino and Alexandre de Moraes Zema absent. The three candidates discussed topics such as the economy, public security and healthcare. The absence of the most prominent frontrunners placed greater spotlight on the smaller parties' voices.

item.title: Renan Santos leva fraldas com nomes de Lula e Flávio em debate e critica ausência em debate
item.description: Renan Santos attended the first presidential debate on Band carrying a diaper printed with the names of Lula and Flávio, symbolizing criticism of their absence. The gesture was interpreted as a direct political provocation toward the candidates who did not show up.

item.title: Horário eleitoral começa nesta semana; Globo entrevistará Lula e Flávio
item.description: The electoral campaign intensifies with the start of free TV and radio advertising on Friday. TV Globo will interview President Lula on Thursday and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro on Friday.

item.title: Lula e Flávio “não sabem explicar os escândalos”, diz Caiado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro's absence from the Band debate, calling them the "most rejected" candidates who cannot explain their scandals. Caiado also previewed that his first economic measure, if elected, would focus on spending control.

item.title: Com Caiado, Renan Santos e Augusto Cury, primeiro debate presidencial tem críticas às ausências de Flávio e Lula
item.description: The first presidential debate was weakened by the absence of Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Zema, with only Caiado, Renan Santos, and Augusto Cury participating. The three candidates criticized the no-shows, highlighting the absentees' reluctance to face accusations and discuss issues like education and public safety.

item.title: Metade dos brasileiros vê risco de interferência estrangeira nas eleições, diz Datafolha
item.description: A new Datafolha survey, filed with the TSE, shows 50% of Brazilians perceive a risk of foreign interference in the 2026 elections. The poll of 2,058 voters was conducted from April 18 to 20, with a maximum margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: No debate da Band, Renan promete estado de defesa contra facções
item.description: In the first televised presidential debate in 2026, promoted by Band, candidate Renan Santos (Missão) stated he plans to declare a state of defense and activate the Law and Order Guarantee in areas dominated by organized crime if elected. The proposal was framed as a measure to combat criminal factions. The debate marked the first TV confrontation between presidential candidates.

item.title: Indecisão de Augusto Cury em debate surpreendeu até equipe do candidato
item.description: Augusto Cury (Avante) nearly withdrew from the first 2026 presidential debate at Band in protest over the absences of Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Romeu Zema. Lula's interview on Record during the debate slot was the final straw. Cury was already leaving when producers convinced him to participate with 15 minutes remaining. Even his running mate, Julio Delgado, was caught off guard and had to turn back.

item.title: Sem Lula, Flávio e Zema, primeiro debate presidencial de 2026 começa esvaziado
item.description: The first presidential debate of 2026, hosted by TV Bandeirantes, opened with only three candidates present: Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos, and Augusto Cury. Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Romeu Zema, who are frontrunners in polls, declined to attend, which may shorten the debate.

item.title: Datafolha: 56% dos eleitores iriam às urnas mesmo se voto não fosse obrigatório
item.description: Datafolha poll reveals 56% of voters would attend polls even without mandatory voting, with higher turnout intent among men, seniors, college-educated, and high-income groups. Supporters of Lula (65%) and Flavio Bolsonaro (62%) show strong voting intentions.

item.title: Augusto Cury desiste de participar de debate na Band
item.description: Augusto Cury, presidential candidate for Avante, withdrew from the Band debate. With his absence, only Renan Santos (Missão) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) confirmed their participation.

item.title: Renan Santos afirma que líderes das pesquisas são 'imbecis corruptos'
item.description: Renan Santos labeled Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro as 'corrupt imbeciles', criticizing their absence from debates. He argued that this stance contradicts the democracy they claim to defend.

item.title: Caiado diz que candidatos ausentes em debate não têm 'nada a mostrar e muito a esconder'
item.description: PSD candidate Ronaldo Caiado criticized the absence of rivals at the TV Bandeirantes and Estadão debate, stating they have 'nothing to show and much to hide'.

item.title: Caiado defende cassação de Lula e Flávio por falta em debate
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado advocates for the cancellation of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro's registrations due to their absence from the first 2026 presidential debate, calling it a disrespect to voters. Romeu Zema also skipped the event, citing Lula's absence. While election law requires invitations, attendance remains voluntary.

item.title: Mais de metade dos eleitores votariam mesmo sem obrigatoriedade, diz Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha poll shows 56% of Brazilians would vote in 2026 elections even without mandatory voting, highest level since 1989. Willingness varies by gender, age, and income, being higher among men (59%), seniors (61%), and high-income voters (75%). Survey interviewed 2,058 people with a two-point margin of error.

item.title: Debate da Band flopou? Lula, Flávio e Zema dão bolo
item.description: The first presidential debate on open TV for the 2026 elections began without three major invited candidates: Lula (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), and Romeu Zema (Novo). Their pre-decided absences raised questions about the relevance of the event hosted by Band.

item.title: Caiado, Renan e Augusto Cury participam de 1º debate presidencial
item.description: The first presidential debate on Band featured only three of the six invited candidates: Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos, and Augusto Cury. Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Romeu Zema chose not to attend. The debate followed a format of direct confrontations and journalist questions.

item.title: Quando começam os debates presidenciais das eleições de 2026?
item.description: The 2026 presidential debates start on Aug 23 on Band, with three more scheduled before the first round. Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) signal they may skip, diminishing debate relevance. Law requires inviting candidates from parties with 5+ federal deputies.

item.title: Kassab nega ter defendido apoio a Lula em segundo turno
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, PSD president and running mate on Ronaldo Caiado's ticket, denied having advocated support for Lula in a potential runoff. Kassab stated Lula would be the best opponent for Caiado in a second-round contest.

item.title: ‘Se está agindo de forma errada, tem que ser investigado’, diz Lula sobre Lulinha
item.description: President Lula stated in an interview with TV Record that his son Fábio Luís da Silva, known as Lulinha, should be investigated if committing wrongdoings, emphasizing that no one is above the law. Lulinha is under investigation for influence trafficking and corruption by the Federal Police and the Supreme Court, linked to the INSS scandal. The statement underscores the government's stance on transparency and rule of law.

item.title: Augusto Cury anuncia que não vai participar de debate da Band
item.description: Augusto Cury (Avante) declined to participate in the Band debate in protest against the absences of Lula (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), and Romeu Zema (Novo). As a result, only Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Renan Santos (Missão) would attend the first 2026 presidential debate.

item.title: Lula e Flávio fugiram do debate por problemas com Dark Horse e Dark Lobby, diz Caiado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro's absence from the 2026 presidential debate, linking it to 'Dark Horse' and 'Dark Lobby' scandals. Romeu Zema and Augusto Cury also skipped the event.

item.title: Debate da Band e do Estadão: se Lula, Flávio e Zema não forem, púlpitos ficarão vazios?
item.description: The first presidential debate of the 2026 race will air Sunday night, hosted by Band and Estadão alongside other outlets. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro have signaled absence, while Zema canceled; only Cury, Renan Santos, and Ronaldo Caiado confirmed. Their podiums will remain empty if they do not attend.

item.title: Lula diz que conversas com Trump são 'civilizadas e respeitosas', mas segundo escalão dos EUA 'toma atitudes impensáveis'
item.description: Lula stated that his conversations with Trump are 'civilized and respectful', but criticized the U.S. 'second tier' for taking 'unthinkable actions', such as imposing tariffs on Brazilian products. In an interview with TV Record, the president said the U.S. allegations justifying the sanctions are 'unfounded' and 'false', mentioning deforestation and slave labor. After a 1h20 phone call between the presidents, Brazil and the U.S. scheduled a meeting for next week between their trade ministers.

item.title: Augusto Cury também não comparece a debate da Band
item.description: Augusto Cury decided not to attend the Band debate, citing the absences of Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Romeu Zema. He went to the network's gate to speak to a small group of supporters waiting for him.

item.title: Kassab afirma que nunca falou de apoio a Lula em eventual 2º turno
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, leader of the PSD and vice-presidential candidate alongside Ronaldo Caiado, denied having stated support for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in a potential runoff election. The statement came amid discussions about alliances and strategies for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Caiado chama Lula e Flávio de “fujões” após ausência em debate
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro's absence from the presidential debate promoted by Band, calling them 'cowards'. Romeu Zema also withdrew from participating after the PT candidate's no-show. The episode highlighted the polarization and evasion of central figures in the race.

item.title: Debate na Band: colunistas do GLOBO comentam o 1º confronto presidencial de 2026; siga ao vivo
item.description: The first 2026 presidential debate, broadcast by Band, featured GLOBO columnists analyzing the absence of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. Zema canceled his participation citing Lula's absence, while Flávio gave a speech in Barretos without concrete proposals for agriculture. Lula denied trying to block investigations into his son and promised punishment if wrongdoing occurred.

item.title: Lula e Flávio deveriam perder registro de candidatura por faltar ao debate, diz Caiado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro's absence from the Band TV debate, stating they should lose their candidacy registration for disrespecting society. Romeu Zema also skipped the event. The former Goiás governor deemed their absence an affront to the Brazilian electorate.

item.title: Debate da Band terá púlpitos vazios para Lula, Flávio e Zema
item.description: Band TV will keep empty podiums in the studio for Lula (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), and Romeu Zema (Novo), who have already confirmed they will not attend the presidential debate this Sunday (23). The event, starting at 8 PM, will feature only Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Renan Santos (Mission) among the announced candidates.

item.title: Renan leva ao debate fraldas com nomes de “Flávio e Lula”
item.description: Renan Santos brought diapers labeled 'Flávio' and 'Lula' to the first presidential debate hosted by Band TV, mocking the absence of both candidates. The act highlights the lack of engagement from the main contenders in the electoral process.

item.title: Com fraldas, Renan Santos chama Lula e Flávio de “criminosos”
item.description: Renan Santos criticized the absence of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in the first presidential debate, calling them criminals and scumbags and bringing symbolic diapers. He cited investigations like Banco Master and INSS, accusing them of organized crime dealings. Other candidates like Romeu Zema also withdrew.

item.title: Em debate da Band, Renan Santos leva fraldas para Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) attended the first Band presidential debate carrying diapers labeled with the names of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), the two main absentees. He accused both of being 'criminals' linked to organized crime and of avoiding the debate out of fear.

item.title: Datafolha: para 50% dos eleitores, há chance de outros países interferirem na eleição brasileira
item.description: A Datafolha survey reveals that 50% of Brazilian voters believe other countries may interfere in the 2026 elections, with 32% viewing it as a problem and 18% not. The poll, conducted between August 18 and 19 with 2,058 respondents, has a margin of error of two percentage points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Lula diz que Lulinha “vai ser punido” se tiver cometido crime e critica entorno de Trump
item.description: President Lula stated that his son Lulinha will be punished if he committed any crime, taking the Federal Police investigations into influence peddling in federal contracts seriously. The probes also involve former chief of staff Marcola and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, suspected of buying jewelry and paying expenses to gain access to Lula's inner circle. Lula declared he does not interfere with the investigations and that 'no one is immune' if they made mistakes.

item.title: Debate presidencial: candidatos se enfrentam na Band; acompanhe
item.description: Lula will skip the presidential debate on Band and instead give an interview to Record at the same time. The candidate confirms he will maintain other media engagements, including an appearance on Globo after the national news.

item.title: Mais de 900 candidatos mudaram declaração de cor entre 2022 e 2026
item.description: A g1 analysis of TSE data shows that 909 out of 6,315 candidates who ran in both 2022 and 2026 changed their declared race or color, representing 14.4% of the sample. The most common shift was from brown to white, with 322 instances.

item.title: Veja como foi o domingo (23) dos candidatos a presidente
item.description: Three candidates participated in the first 2026 presidential debate promoted by Band TV, while others held political or religious events or had no public schedule. Zema and Marçal stood out by withdrawing from the debate and being barred from campaigning, respectively. Issues such as housing, healthcare, and education were discussed, especially by Hertz Dias.
